body.claim: A warm charger is not losing energy for nothing: some of it is being transformed into heat.
body.why: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed or transferred. Current through any conductor produces heat, with heating power equal to the resistance times the square of the current. In older adapters the losses in the transformer and regulator were considerable, and significant power was dissipated as heat even with no load.

probes.question: A charger warms up as it works. Where does that heat energy come from?
options: It is converted from electrical energy
It is absorbed from the air

probes.question: True or false: Joule's law says heating power equals resistance times the square of the current.

claims.claim: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed or transferred (probe 1)
claims.quote: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; rather, it can only be transformed or transferred from one form to another.

claims.claim: Current through a conductor produces heat (heat comes from electrical energy)
claims.quote: the passage of an electric current through a conductor produces heat

claims.claim: Heating power equals resistance times square of current (probe 2)
claims.quote: states that the power of heating generated by an electrical conductor equals the product of its resistance and the square of the current

claims.claim: Older adapters: transformer and regulator losses were considerable
claims.quote: Losses in the transformer and the linear regulator were considerable

claims.claim: Significant power dissipated as heat even with no load
claims.quote: significant power dissipated as heat even when not driving a load
